comment: NPC wardrobe slots (cosmos_chimera docs/design/npc-uma-looks.md#服裝, row 17), built by npc_outfit.py (pieces, trims) and npc_cut.py (cuts) on both bases of every race below: what NpcMeshes Signature (piece_<ArchRegion>), the era block of Dress (trim_<ArchEra>) and Dress itself (the cuts) draw, refitted to the base's body. Agrarian and Mercantile have no trim (their era shows in the cut and sleeves).
races_comment: Every race the game assembles on UMA (NpcMeshes.UmaCarries): skeletons, automata and crabfolk stay procedural and, the first two, unclothed.

cuts.comment: Q-A26 = A. Mirrored by NpcMeshes.GarmentFitOf (cosmos_chimera): change both. top: one slot per cut and the sleeve lengths it can be drawn with (NpcMeshes Dress: robes and coats force long sleeves, labourers go bare, wraps reach short at most); hem (share of the leg below the hip) and ease (procedural fit) are the shape keys npc_hem / npc_ease, 0 at the low end and 1 at the high end. Era hems 0.06-0.8 x lerp(0.78, 1.14, Textile01); dress, vest and coat clamp them; wrap fixes it; the robe top stops at 0.12 over its ankle-long skirt, which carries the braid (NpcMeshes hangs both, hem 0.9 and fall 0.93, which would cross). skirt: fall (share of the leg) and flare, keys npc_fall / npc_flare. legs: trouser ease. boots: height as the share of ankle to knee / 1.6, per lower era (ancient wears the industrial pair; primal goes barefoot).
